facts.statement: Velocipes means "quick foot" and is a Late Triassic saurischian dinosaur that may have been a theropod.
facts.quote: Velocipes (meaning "quick foot") is a genus of saurischian dinosaur from the Late Triassic that may have been a theropod.

facts.statement: The type species Velocipes guerichi was first described by Huene in 1932 based on a poorly preserved fibula discovered in southern Poland around 1884.
facts.quote: The type species, V. guerichi, was first described by Huene in 1932 as a coelurosaur, based on GPIM UH no. 252, which consists of the proximal portion of a very poorly preserved fibula that was discovered in the Lissauer Breccia of Kocury, southern Poland by Georg Gürich around 1884

facts.statement: The fossil bone was described but not named until 1884.
facts.quote: the bone was described but not named in 1884

facts.statement: The fossil bone was thought to be destroyed after damage during World War II until it was rediscovered in 2012.
facts.quote: The bone was damaged during the Second World War and was thought to have been destroyed until it was rediscovered in 2012 by D. Mazurek.

facts.statement: In 1956, Velocipes was placed in the Halticosauridae, a family that later became monotypic.
facts.quote: In 1956, von Huene placed Velocipes in the Halticosauridae, which has since become monotypic to only include Halticosaurus.

facts.statement: In 1984, Samuel Paul Welles suggested that Velocipes might be synonymous with Liliensternus.
facts.quote: In 1984, Samuel Paul Welles considered Velocipes to be synonymous with Liliensternus.

facts.statement: Recent studies consider Velocipes to be a basal neotheropod or closely related to that clade.
facts.quote: The authors considered Velocipes to have been a basal neotheropod or a taxon closely related to this clade.

facts.statement: The surviving fibula fragment is 16.4 cm long, suggesting the full bone was roughly 30-35 cm.
facts.quote: The surviving portion of the fibula is 16.4 cm long and after comparing the bone to other related theropods, it is believed that the full fibula was roughly 30-35 cm in length.

facts.statement: The fibula has a concave medial surface and a lateral ridge measuring about 52 mm long and 5 mm high.
facts.quote: The medial surface is slightly concave, suggesting that Velocipes may have been a neotheropod, and on the lateral surface of the bone there is a clear ridge about 52 mm long and about 5 mm high.

facts.statement: Based on the fibula size, Velocipes may have reached up to 3 meters long and weighed around 50 kg, though this is speculative due to the single known specimen.
facts.quote: It is assumed that, based on the estimated size of the fibula, Velocipes may have reached up to 3 m long and weighed around 50 kg, although this can only be speculated as only one specimen of Velocipes is currently known to exist.

facts.statement: Velocipes fossils were found in the Norian-aged Lissauer Breccia of southern Poland.
facts.quote: Its fossils were found in the Norian-aged Lissauer Breccia of southern Poland.

facts.statement: Velocipes lived during the Norian stage, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Velocipes lived alongside the aetosaur Kocurypelta, an indeterminate lungfish, and the stem-turtle Proterochersis.
facts.quote: Velocipes would have been contemporaneous with the aetosaur genus Kocurypelta, an indeterminate species of lungfish, and the stem-turtle Proterochersis cf. porebensis.

rejected.statement: In 2000, Rauhut and Hungerbuhler argued the specimen was too poorly preserved to identify as a fibula and classified the genus as an indeterminate vertebrate.
rejected.quote: A later paper, published in 2000 by Rauhut and Hungerbuhler, claimed that the only specimen of this animal was not well preserved enough to be confidently identified as part of a fibula, and classified the genus as an "indeterminate vertebrate".
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'fibula and classified the genus as an indeterminate'

rejected.statement: In 2004, Tykoski and Rowe listed Velocipes as a possible ceratosaur or coelophysoid.
rejected.quote: In 2004, Ronald Tykoski and Timothy Rowe listed Velocipes as a possible ceratosaur or coelophysoid.
